verbs.description: Copy a vault item's secret Puts one secret of an item on its person's clipboard, which forgets it again after a while, written down as a use. The secret is answered to nobody: the device that keeps the vault copies it.
verbs.label: Copy a vault item's secret

verbs.description: Show a vault item's secret Answers one secret of an item to its person, to be shown while they look, as `Revealed`, written down as a use. No record of the call keeps it.
verbs.label: Show a vault item's secret

verbs.description: Ask your person for a secret Ask your person for a password, a key or another secret. This is the one way to get one: never ask for one in the conversation, where everyone in it and you read what they write. Your person types it into the system's protected field on their own device, in words the system writes; you never see it. The workspace's vault keeps it for the places in `belongsTo` alone: a site as `https://example.com`, a server as `imap://mail.example.com:993` or `ssh://git.example.com`. You are told the `reference` it is kept under (`vault.item:…`), or that they declined: pass the reference where an action takes the secret. Where nobody watches, the call ends at once and you are told in your conversation with them; do not make it again.
verbs.label: Ask your person for a secret

verbs.description: Fill page field from vault Fill a field of a web page from an item your person's vault keeps for that page's site: a login's password, a code generator's code of this moment, or a kept value. You never see what the item keeps. When you work with nobody watching, your person is asked first in the conversation whether you may use the item there: tell them it waits for their answer and do not make the call again. The item is used when they allow it, and after their Always without asking.
verbs.label: Fill page field from vault

verbs.description: Call a service with a key from the vault Make a web request to a service that takes a key, with a key your person's vault keeps: for a service that has no connection of its own. The server adds the key on the way out, where the item says its service takes it (as a bearer token unless it says otherwise), and only to the service the item belongs to: `url` must be at that service's web address, over https. You never see the key, and it is struck from what you are answered: the status, the headers and the body. What it sends is `body` text, `bodyParts` (an inline `text` or `json` part, or a `content` part naming content your workspace keeps by its BLAKE3 hex address, with its filename and content type), or `bodyContent`, one content reference sent as the whole body. The server reads that content from the workspace's store: its bytes never pass through you, and you may name only content the workspace keeps. To get the key, call the vault's `ask` with kind `key`, belongsTo `["<the service's web address, such as https://api.example.com>"]` and `sentIn`, which says how the service takes its key when not as a bearer token: `basic`, `header:<name>` such as `header:X-Api-Key`, or `query:<name>`. Your person types it into a protected field, and you are told the `reference` the workspace's vault keeps it under. Pass that reference as `key`. When you work with nobody watching, your person is asked first in the conversation whether you may make this call, and nothing is sent: tell them it waits for their answer. Once they allowed it, make the same call again with the same arguments: it is sent once. Each call is asked about anew.
verbs.label: Call a service with a key from the vault

verbs.description: Read a code from the vault The code of this moment from a code generator's seed, addressed at the item (`vault.item:<id>#code`), so a grant covers that one account. It is a read: the vault computes it where the seed is and writes nothing down, so it appears in no change, no use and no history.
verbs.label: Read a code from the vault

verbs.description: Sign with an ssh key from the vault Signs with the ssh key an item keeps, for one of the ssh servers it belongs to, addressed at the item (`vault.item:<id>#sign`), so a grant covers that one key. The vault signs where the key is and answers the signature and the key's public line; the private key never leaves it. Each signature is a use the item remembers.
verbs.label: Sign with an ssh key from the vault

verbs.description: Hand a vault item's secret to an app's process Hands one item's secret to a process of an app's own that speaks the item's protocol itself (a gateway login, voice, an SSH or VNC handshake, a database login), addressed at the item (`vault.item:<id>#release`), so the grant its person gives on it is a grant on that item alone. Only the app's own connection is answered, and nothing keeps the secret: no record, argument, log or history.
verbs.label: Hand a vault item's secret to an app's process

verbs.description: Find an app's vault item Finds the item a moved app's secret was kept as, by the app and purpose tags the app names, answering its reference as `Found`. It is answered only to that app's own connection, never to a person, a page or an agent.
verbs.label: Find an app's vault item

schema.description: What `FIND` answers: the item's reference, or `None` when the vault keeps no item tagged with that app and purpose.

verbs.description: Keep an app's own secret Keeps a secret an app obtained or made itself, such as an OAuth token or a key it generated, in the workspace's vault as that app's own, answering the item's reference as `Kept`. It is answered only on the app's own connection: the app is the one that connection was placed for, never an argument.
verbs.label: Keep an app's own secret

schema.description: What `KEEP` answers: the reference of the item the secret is kept as.

verbs.description: Read this device's key for an app The key this device derives for an app and a purpose of its own, as 32 bytes of lowercase hex: what identifies the app's install on this device to a service that pairs with devices. The device's daemon derives it from the device's own key, so it is the same for the same app and purpose on this device, differs on every other device, and is kept nowhere.
verbs.label: Read this device's key for an app

verbs.description: List a site's logins The logins the vault keeps for one site, as `PageLogins`: what is safe to say of each, the name it signs in with included, never its secret. It and the other page login actions are answered only to a window of an app's own that shows a page, on that window's own connection.
verbs.label: List a site's logins
